How Rain, Rock, and Myth Gave Birth to Civilization

In the eastern highlands of modern-day Turkey, a ragged wall of limestone and basalt separates the Anatolian valleys from the flat plains of Mesopotamia. For millennia, these peaks—soaring over three thousand meters into the sky—have trapped rainclouds drifting in from Asia to the east and the Indian Ocean to the south.

Unable to clear the towering ridges, the clouds wander instead through the valleys and gorges carved deep into the range. Warm air rising from the southern deserts collides with them, packing them even denser and unleashing unusually heavy, thunderous rainfall—especially in spring and summer.

In short

  • The Taurus Mountains trapped rainclouds and fed the Tigris and Euphrates, turning southern Iraq's barren desert into fertile silt plains.
  • Early highland hunter-gatherers domesticated wild crops around 11,000 BCE, built monuments like Göbekli Tepe, and later migrated south during the Ubaid period (6500–5500 BCE).
  • Post–Ice Age sea-level rise flooded a fertile Persian Gulf valley, driving flood-haunted migrants northward into southern Mesopotamia—the mysterious Sumerians.
  • Settling alongside the Semitic-speaking Akkadians, the Sumerians mastered irrigation, founded Eridu around 5400 BCE, and laid the foundations of urban civilization.

The Mountains That Trapped the Sky

The Taurus Mountains trapped drifting rainclouds for millennia, nourishing the green arc of the Fertile Crescent.

Before cities, before kings, even before farming, the Taurus Mountains shaped human destiny. A simple accident of geography—stone walls catching passing clouds—changed everything. For thousands of years, those trapped rains sustained a lush green arc across an otherwise unforgiving landscape: the Fertile Crescent.

Here, in this crescent of green sculpted by rock and water, humans took their first steps toward civilization. Tens of thousands of years before our own species settled these slopes, the valleys were already alive with archaic humans. Archaeological traces of Homo erectus show that they roamed these ridges nearly half a million years ago. Our direct ancestors, Homo sapiens, followed, drawn by abundant game, fresh water, and fertile ground.

Storm Gods, Bulls, and Thunderous Rain (Before 11,000 BCE)

The heavy mountain rains fed subterranean lakes and small highland streams that gathered into rushing tributaries. Over geological time, rivers pouring out of these highlands carved canyons, wore down limestone ridges, and carried vast quantities of fine silt southward. Silt-rich soil is remarkably good at holding moisture while still letting air circulate—an ideal cradle for crops.

Reinforced by meltwater from the snowcapped Caucasus Mountains to the northeast, these waters formed two legendary rivers: the Tigris and the Euphrates. Their floodplains became the lifeblood of the south, a region that would otherwise be little more than an inhospitable desert. Season after season, the rivers sculpted the lowlands, spreading rich silt across wide plains and laying the groundwork for what would become Mesopotamia.

Water shaped not only the terrain, but also the inner world of its earliest people. The name "Taurus" comes from the Latin word for bull—a fitting echo of the terracotta bull figurines unearthed across the region. Early hunter-gatherers worshipped the storm god Teshub, believing he rode an enormous bull and thundered across the heavens. The roar of summer storms rolling through the gorges must have sounded like hooves galloping overhead—a divine reminder that rain was at once a gift and a threat.

From Hunter-Gatherers to the First Farmers (11,000–6500 BCE)

For most of prehistory, humans survived by hunting and gathering, moving as the seasons and herds demanded. Early Neolithic hunter-gatherers preferred the foothills of the northern mountains, where the climate was temperate, rainfall was plentiful, and wild resources were abundant.

Around 11,000 BCE, however, everything began to shift. Somewhere in the Anatolian highlands, people noticed something extraordinary: discarded seeds from edible wild plants were sprouting in their rubbish heaps. Over generations, they realized that by burying seeds, watering them, and tending the earth, they could grow food on purpose. That quiet discovery altered the entire arc of human history.

Göbekli Tepe, built around 9600 BCE—millennia before the pyramids of Egypt or the stones of Stonehenge.

Where families had once wandered with herds and changing seasons, they now built permanent homes beside their fields. They clustered into villages, erected granaries to carry them through winter, shaped clay into cooking pots, and began to worship together. Monumental sanctuaries rose, too. The unearthed megalithic site of Göbekli Tepe, built around 9600 BCE, reveals the remarkable sophistication of these early communities—some 4,000 years before the Sumerians first reached southern Iraq, roughly 6,000 years before the first stones of Stonehenge, and more than 7,000 years before Egypt's earliest pyramids.

The Rivers That Gave Life

The vast floodplain of the Tigris and Euphrates is known today as Iraq—or Bilad al-Rafidayn in Arabic, "the land of the two rivers." Yet we remember its ancient world more commonly by its Greek name: Mesopotamia, from mesos ("between") and potamos ("river"). For thousands of years, those two great arteries carried silt down from the Taurus Mountains, transforming not only an arid desert landscape, but the entire trajectory of human life.

Hot, parched southern Mesopotamia is, on paper, the last place on Earth one might expect a civilization to begin. Beyond the green ribbon created by the twin rivers and their southern delta, southern Iraq is an unforgiving desert. It holds almost no raw materials: no timber, no building stone, no metal ores. Summers are searing, the winds are fierce, and rain barely falls.

Because the rivers depended on highland rain and snowmelt, their floods were notoriously unpredictable. Years of deluge were often followed by years of drought. Early farmers wisely stayed in the northern foothills, where rain fell reliably and resources were close at hand. For millennia, before the Sumerians and Akkadians made it their home, southern Mesopotamia remained little more than a flat expanse of clay and silt.

Migration to the South: The Ubaid Period (6500–5500 BCE)

For several thousand years, agriculture remained largely a highland affair. Yet as both populations and farming expertise grew in the northern foothills, communities began to fan out in search of new arable land.

Over those same millennia, the Tigris and Euphrates had quietly turned the barren flats of southern Iraq into rich alluvial plains. By around 6500 BCE, waves of early pioneers pushed southward, drawn by that fertile frontier. Archaeologists call this era—roughly 6500 to 5500 BCE—the Ubaid period, named after Tell al-Ubaid, the site where its distinctive artifacts were first uncovered.

These settlers adapted to their stark new environment with remarkable ingenuity. Lacking timber, they built houses from bundled reeds harvested in the southern marshes. They threw up earthen dams and dug the first irrigation canals, taming the rivers' erratic floods and guiding water onto their fields. In those reclaimed plots, they cultivated wheat, millet, sesame, and rye.

Ubaid terracotta figurines (circa 6000 BCE), relics of the earliest farmers to settle southern Mesopotamia.

Moving downriver, they also encountered date palms lining the banks, with broad fronds and sweet fruit. Drawn by the shade those trees offered, they learned to plant palms in their gardens and grow pomegranates and figs beneath their canopy. They developed the potter's wheel and elevated clay into fine vessels.

Who exactly these Ubaid pioneers were—what language they spoke, what gods they honored, or what they called themselves—remains a mystery. Whether they were the direct ancestors of the Semitic-speaking Akkadians who later rose in the north is still an open question.

Just like the two great rivers, two distinct peoples soon came to share the land between the waters. To the north lived the Akkadians, speakers of a Semitic tongue who carried forward the Ubaid way of life. To the south, near the marshy seacoast, lived the far more enigmatic Sumerians.

Living intertwined and side by side, these two peoples forged humanity's first true civilization in southern Iraq—a cultural continuum that endured for an astonishing three and a half millennia, from around 5400 BCE until its final collapse around 1750 BCE.

People of the Great Flood

The Sumerian memory of history was haunted by an event of apocalyptic scale. According to their legends, their ancestors had fled a catastrophic deluge that swallowed their entire homeland. This "Great Flood" may be the oldest continuously told story in human memory—later echoed in Babylonian epics, Hebrew scripture, and even Greek myth.

Today, the Tigris and Euphrates flow roughly two thousand kilometers from the Taurus Mountains before emptying into the Persian Gulf in southern Iraq. Before the end of the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) around 10,000 BCE, however, the two rivers did not end where they do now. They joined in southern Iraq into a single mighty waterway that wound across what is now the bed of the Persian Gulf, traveling another six hundred kilometers before reaching the Indian Ocean near modern-day Dubai.

The low-lying river valley that once stretched across the Persian Gulf basin before post–Ice Age seas submerged it (circa 12,000 BCE).

That ancient river would have nourished a lush floodplain between Iran and Saudi Arabia—a low-lying valley now buried beneath the Persian Gulf. In deep prehistory, Neolithic communities descending from the Iranian highlands may have settled this sheltered basin, living for millennia in near-complete isolation from the peoples of the Fertile Crescent.

Then the Ice Age ended. As global temperatures climbed by 4 to 7°C between roughly 10,000 and 5000 BCE, northern ice sheets melted and global sea levels rose by an astounding 120 meters. This was the same planetary transformation that submerged the land bridges linking Britain to continental Europe and Siberia to Alaska.

The sea rose slowly at first, then relentlessly, devouring vast stretches of low-lying land across the globe. For anyone dwelling in the Persian Gulf basin, the encroaching ocean was an apocalypse in slow motion. Over five thousand years, the water claimed the valley at a startling pace—roughly a meter every three days, about 120 meters every year, and a full kilometer every decade.

For the communities living there, the rising tide must have felt both devastating and unstoppable. Century after century, they were forced northward as waves swallowed their forests, fields, and villages. Crowded into ever-denser settlements along the retreating shoreline, they had to improvise and adapt at every step before the sea advanced again.

That long exodus pushed inland until global temperatures stabilized and the coastline reached its furthest northward extent around 5500–5000 BCE.

The Sumerian Problem: Strangers With an Alien Tongue

Between 5500 and 5000 BCE, the Sumerians appeared along the southern marshes of Iraq, carrying stories of a great flood that had drowned their ancestors' world. They also brought a language so unlike any around them that archaeologists have long called it the "Sumerian Problem."

Unlike Akkadian, Babylonian, or later Aramaic—all members of the Semitic language family—Sumerian is what linguists call a language isolate. It shares no proven kinship with any other known tongue on Earth. Having lived in isolation for millennia, the Sumerians spoke a language entirely distinct from the Semitic peoples of the northern plains. When nineteenth-century scholars first uncovered cuneiform tablets written in Sumerian, they assumed they were looking at a cryptic Babylonian code—until they realized they had stumbled upon something far older and altogether different.

Whether they arrived by sea or retreated north ahead of the rising Gulf, the Sumerians brought a distinct language and deep mythic memory.

Some theories have even suggested that the Sumerians arrived by boat from distant lands such as India. Sumerian myth spoke of the god Enki creating humankind in a faraway paradise called Dilmun, often linked with modern Bahrain. Later Babylonian lore told of Oannes, an amphibious sage who emerged from the sea to teach humanity the arts of civilization before returning to the waves.

Whether they sailed in from afar or walked north out of a drowned Persian Gulf valley remains uncertain. Still, it is entirely plausible that these myths preserve a distant echo of the Sumerians' arrival on the marshy shores of southern Iraq.

Around 5500 BCE, as Semitic-speaking communities moved down from the northern foothills onto the riverbanks, they met these flood-scarred newcomers pressing up from the south—people who carried memories of a vanished world along with a remarkably advanced culture and ingenious ideas.

The two peoples settled in parallel, much like the rivers themselves: Akkadians to the north, Sumerians to the south. Living side by side, trading, borrowing ideas, and sharing both triumphs and setbacks, they forged a symbiotic partnership that lasted more than three and a half thousand years and gave birth to the first civilization in human history.

The Birth of Civilization: The First Sumerian Settlements

According to Sumerian tradition, kingship first descended from heaven in the city of Eridu, founded around 5400 BCE near the ancient seacoast. At its height, Eridu may have housed 10,000 people—an extraordinary concentration of humanity for its age.

While the Sumerians' ultimate origins remain misty, we know a great deal about who they were and how they lived. They imagined the world as a circular landmass ringed by bitter seas, with fresh water from rivers and rain welling at its heart. They called their homeland Ki-en-gir—"the land of the noble lords." Their own civilized heartland was Kalam; the wild, untamed territories beyond were Kur.

They called themselves Uĝ saĝ gíg ga—"the black-haired people"—setting themselves apart from the Akkadians on the northern plains. From ancient carvings, we can even see what they wore. Ordinary men and women dressed in sheepskin kilts accented with copper and iron jewelry, while the wealthy wore dyed woolen robes trimmed with gold. They styled their hair curly on top and cropped short along the sides.

They brought musical instruments with them, too—and remarkably, we can still hear echoes of their sound today. Just as they recorded trade and myth, they wrote down musical instructions explaining how to tune and play their instruments.

A Sumerian cuneiform clay tablet (circa 3100 BCE), part of the world's earliest known writing tradition.

With almost no stone or timber, the Sumerians built a civilization out of mud and water. From clay they fashioned nearly everything—cooking pots, harvest sickles, and writing tablets. They molded bricks from river mud and wove roofs from marsh reeds. Their mudbrick houses often featured intricate arches and domes, and families frequently slept on their rooftops at night to escape the desert heat.

From clay, reeds, and copper, Sumerian artisans built vaulted homes, wheeled carts, sailboats, and thriving workshops.

They refined the potter's wheel, invented the plow and the wagon wheel, spun wool and plant fibers, learned to cast copper and later bronze, and built sailboats to ride the river currents.

They also invented mathematics we still live by. The 360 degrees of a circle come directly from Sumer. Their base-60 number system survives every time we glance at a clock—sixty minutes in an hour, sixty seconds in a minute. By counting the three knuckle segments on each of the four fingers of one hand with their thumb, they reached twelve; multiplying by the five fingers of the other hand gave them sixty.

Their most transformative invention, however, was large-scale irrigation. Vast networks of canals and dikes pushed farmland deep into the desert, while dams tamed spring floods and stored water to carry communities through dry seasons. Those same canals doubled as highways of commerce, floating grain and goods between settlements.

Bit by bit, the face of southern Iraq changed—from dusty desert and tangled marshland into lush green fields. Powered by that ingenuity, Sumerian society expanded at a slow, steady rhythm.

Intricate canal networks turned unpredictable seasonal floods into reliable harvests and bustling trade routes.

Eridu and the Dawn of the First Cities

Ingenuity, sharpened by the demands of a harsh desert, gradually gave rise to an ever more complex society. Digging and maintaining miles of irrigation canals required careful planning, engineering skill, and mathematical calculation. Work gangs had to be organized and paid in rations of food and beer; foremen and overseers had to be appointed. Out of that logistical necessity grew early bureaucracy—and with it, the world's first true states.

In Sumerian memory, Eridu stood first among them all. Founded around 5400 BCE near the Persian Gulf coast, it grew to roughly 10,000 inhabitants—a staggering figure for its era. Soon a whole constellation of small cities dotted southern Iraq. Each independent city clustered around its central temple and was governed by a priest-king known as an ensi, often advised by a council of elders that included both men and women.

Eridu, revered by later Sumerians as the first city where kingship descended from heaven.

By about 5000 BCE, Sumerian cities had eclipsed the older Ubaid culture. Remarkably, this dawn of urban life—known as the Eridu period (5400–3900 BCE)—remained largely peaceful for nearly 1,500 years. There is little archaeological evidence of warfare or standing armies, and most towns stood without defensive walls. Yet as populations swelled and wealth concentrated, inequality deepened. The earliest traces of slavery appear in this very era—a dark shadow that would lengthen across the centuries.

Over the next few centuries, the Sumerians remained relatively insulated, seldom venturing far into the surrounding Kur. As their cities matured, however, so did their ambition and reach. Soon they would invent writing, sail their reed and timber boats as far as Africa and India, trade along routes stretching from Cyprus to Afghanistan, and raise grand metropolises like Ur and Uruk.

That next chapter—the Uruk Period (3900–2400 BCE)—would carry Sumer from a primordial river society into humanity's first truly urban civilization.

link.title: Between Two Rivers: How Mesopotamia Gave Birth to Civilization

उसका पातहरूमा - लेखिएका छन् घामका अक्षर। उसको मुटुमा - कुँदिएका छन् घामकै छायाँ। उसको गन्धमा - घुलिएका छन् घामको सम्झना। उ देखिएन भने पनि बाँच्छ, उ बुझिएन भने पनि बोल्छ।

घाम त
आखिर घाम नै हो -
उसको त धर्म नै हो
आफ्नै आगोमा अनवरत जल्ने,
टाढैबाट चम्केर उज्यालो छर्ने।

उसको कर्म नै हो -
सारा सृष्टिलाई सुनौलो पार्ने,
अनन्त आकाश छिचोल्दै
निरन्तर अघि बढिरहने।

घाम टाढा छे -
आकाशको अर्को पाटामा,
बादलको अँगालोभित्र बस्छे।
ऊ आफैं जल्छे,
आफैं चम्किन्छे,
आफ्नै मुस्कान आफैंलाई बाँड्छे;
रातको अर्धविराम चिरेर
बिहान अझ प्रखर फक्रन्छे।

फूल त
आखिर फूल नै हो -
माटोको आत्मामा टाँसिएको,
उसको त रहरनै हुन्छ-
घामकै आशामा फुलिरहने,
ओइलिने नियत बुझेर पनि
फुल्ने रहर मार्न नसक्ने।

उसका पातहरूमा -
लेखिएका छन् घामका अक्षर।
उसको प्राणहरू -
जलेका छन् घामकै नाममा।
उसको जीवन -
बगेको छ उज्यालोको प्रतीक्षामा ।
उसको मुटुमा -
कुँदिएका छन् घामकै छायाँ।
उसको गन्धमा -
घुलिएका छन् घामको सम्झना।
उ देखिएन भने पनि बाँच्छ,
उ बुझिएन भने पनि बोल्छ।

घामले थाहा नपाए पनि
फूलको आँखा सधैं घामकै बाटो कुर्छ;
रातको अँध्यारोले छोप्दा
बिहान फेरि फक्रिने आशामा
एक तमास आँखा चिम्लन्छ,
उज्यालोको प्रतीक्षामा रात बाँच्छ।

रात पर्छ,
बादल टाँसिन्छन्,
साँझ तारा ओर्लँदा
फूल आफूलाई सम्झाउँछ -
घामको न्यानोले मात्रै होइन,
उसको टाढाइले पनि
फूललाई जिउँदो राख्छ।

र बिहान -
घामको एउटा झुल्को उज्यालोले
उसको पर्खाइ रोकिन्छ,
रातहरू उज्यालो हुन्छन्,
रंग फेरिन्छ,
उ आँखा खोल्छ,
र आफ्ना रंगहरू
फेरि एकपटक घामलाई चढाउँछ।

फूल बुझ्छ -
घामले शायद कहिल्यै
उसको मुटुको कम्पन सुन्नेछैन,
तर ऊ अझै घामकै लागि
रंगहरू चढाउँछ,
गन्ध बाँच्छ,
र आफ्ना सपनाहरू जलाउँछ।

घामकै नाममा ओइलिनु पनि
प्रेमको एउटा रूप हो।

अनि कहिलेकाहीँ -
बादलले छेकिएर सही
घामको नजर केही क्षण फूलमाथि पर्यो भने,
फूलको सम्पूर्ण ब्रह्माण्ड उज्यालिन्छ;
घामलाई थाहा हुँदैन
उसको एक झिल्काले
फूलको आत्मा फेरि फक्रन्छ।

अस्तित्वभन्दा बाहिरको विश्वास,
टाढैबाट पूजा गर्ने साहस,
घामले देख्ला कि नदेख्ला भन्ने डरमै
फुलिरहने आत्मा।

घामकै नाममा फक्रँदै
घामकै नाममा ओइलिनु पर्ने नियति।

घाम उदाउँछ र अस्ताउँछ,
फूल फुल्छ र ओइलिन्छ;
त्यसैले घाम र फूलको कथा
कहिल्यै पूरा हुँदैन -
कविताजस्तै -
शब्द सकिए पनि भाव बाँकी रहने,
रात ओइलिँदा पनि आशा बाँकी रहने।

घाम त आखिर घाम नै हो -
टाढैबाट जलिरहने;
र फूल त आखिर फूल नै हो -
घामकै लागि फुलिरहने।

stay, alive in my head a little longer. stay, so that I may go on writing poems against forgetting. stay, so, I may keep on living fighting for surviving.

I was not her mirror,
nor she mine.
we were not possessions-
not the kind the world wraps
in vows and velvet.

but for a while,
we lived-
we breathed-
we exhaled the same wind
we burned-
on the same trembling planet
under the same pale sky.

two ghosts of light-
crossing paths,
that was enough
to rupture the dark.

but for a flicker-
a breath,
a shared orbit of quiet mornings
and crooked shadows.
for one absurd
infinitesimal moment,
we existed-
on this strange blue planet,
two mistakes in time
that almost rhyme.

and somehow,
it was enough
to make the silence
inside me hum like a hymn.
haunt me beautiful,
haunt me beautifully.

I was never hers
and she was never mine,
she is not someone
who belongs to anyone.

she was the kind of woman
you don’t wait for-
you just feel lucky
she walked past.
she is-
the dry rustle and torn pages
of forgotten books.

the wildness of flowers-
that grow without gardens
and find their way,
in the broken pavements
the ones who dare the wind.

she haunts me gently-
her shadow in my room
and her ghost in my bones
not as a scream,
but as the hush
between waves,
like blood songs in my veins.

sweating with memory,
drencheched in what ifs,
like how the wind remembers
the shape of a window
long after it’s shut.

drenched in something
almost holy,
that was enough
to make my skin feel
like it belonged to something.

now I carry the ghost of her
not with blooming roses
not in longing,
no possession.
only presence-
a rebellion,
tender and unfinished.

We did not belong,
not in the way letters
find envelopes,
or raindrops cling to glass.

because love-
real love-
doesn’t always
need a return address.
sometimes it just needs
a corner of your gut
that hurts good.

haunt me beautiful.
haunt me
like moonlight stays
on rooftops no one looks at.

and perhaps that is all
we are allowed-
to hurt beautifully
for what never had
the weight we bear
just to exist.

and so, I walk,
with a heavy heart,
through room of thoughts
with all her echo.
all I ask-
stay blooming in my skull
just a moment longer.

because love,
real love-
even unspoken,
even unwelcome,
can sting so sweet
you are born a lazarus
once you learn to rise again.

stay,
alive in my head a little longer.
stay,
so that I may go on writing poems
against forgetting.
stay,
so, I may keep on living
fighting for surviving.

blue, something about you, woke up with thoughts of you, crossed my mind as the storms come through, chaos and calm, bliss and peace, starry nights, and northern lights, folded dreams, holy grails, loud laughs and…

blue,
something about you,
woke up with thoughts of you,
crossed my mind as the storms come through,
chaos and calm, bliss and peace,
starry nights, and northern lights,
folded dreams, holy grails,
loud laughs and little blushes,
sunset hues- a little close/closer to blue,
sweet loving hell- you get me through.
silly songs and foggy lullabies,
all my words speak of you.
oh blue- i love you.

i woke up dreaming of blue
sad eyes are going to be the ruins of me,
it feels a little dark but i am alright babe,
my feelings will learn to cope.
tiny dreams pretty whims-
midnight ocean, sloppy kisses,
good memories have endless riches,
little moment that lasts the ages.
wishes you wishes were true. blue
oh blue.. words don’t come through.

in the end,
it is dreams, poetry, sunsets,
mountain-blues, a kindred soul
we all have affairs with beautiful things,
the world needs more happy endings-
but-
time’s a storm and ours was just a fling,
it’s alright blue,
some wings aren’t meant to swing.

do i deserve to write about you,
does she deserve me writing about her,
none of us are in control,
moments to memories,
biffs and bliss,
it has been a strange flight, (still is)
there is always a home for you in my chest,
and yet-
fading away seems like the best thing to do,
blue.. oh blue, ode to you.

title.$t: she is not here- but she is everywhere.

content.$t:
sunshine- in human form. knowing she exists, here. now. in this universe- somewhere, anywhere. too holy to touch, too human to forget. not to be held- to be known. and that knowing, softens me. my being. this joy- only…

she is not here-
but she is everywhere.

not in a time,
not in a place,
not a face,
not a name,
not a story,
not even
a memory
i can tell.

just in
her being.
she’s out
there-
somewhere.

no longer
waiting
for a when.
no longer
wondering
for a where.
no more
questions:
where,
how,
who,
or if.

regardless of-
who she is,
where she is,
how she is-
whenever,
wherever,
however,
whether,
if-
she exists.

sunshine-
in human form.
knowing
she exists,
here. now.
in this universe-
somewhere,
anywhere.

too holy
to touch,
too human
to forget.
not to be held-
to be known.

and that knowing,
softens me.
my being.

this joy-
only
a feeling,
only
for her existing.

this joy-
is mine.
for nothing,
and for everything.

it lasts-
for however
long
it wants,
if there
is a start.
if there is
a beginning
or an ending.

i am-
no longer-
alone in
this universe,
wondering
whether
she exists.

all this
happiness-
because
she exists.

“You are
your own fire.
hold on-
even when
the world burns.”

in this Universe,
March 11, 2025

content.$t:
now, it barely stands. weathering the weather, a far cry from the majesty it once bore.

across the street
from where i grew up-
lies an old house,
rotting in its own silence.

paint peels like brittle skin,
windows nailed shut,
a monument
to a bygone era.

it has seen better days,
once stood tall, proud-
boasting more rooms
than people to fill them.
they say
it was the first concrete house
in the village.

an old couple lived there,
with their quiet maids,
beyond the hush
of long corridors.
stories were whispered-
tales of riches,
gold and jewels,
tucked in suitcases,
hidden in the ceilings.

it was the ’90s,
and they had the only tv
in the village.
a black-and-white box
locked in a wooden cabinet,
untouched,
sacred-
like a relic
no one dared disturb.

every saturday morning
they’d ask the maids
to bring the TV down
like a holy offering.
we’d gather,
sit cross-legged on cold floors,
and watch ramayana
in silence,

then one day-
the wife died,
just like that.
and everything changed.

i don’t know
if the children told the old man,
or raided the ceilings first-
i was young to know.
but i heard:
the suitcases held
nothing but rats,
and the jewels
were only silver.

the old man followed soon after.
the house remained-
empty and stark,
a relic left
to mourn itself.

no one returned.
no one repaired.
years passed.
and the old tv
was never
brought down again.

all that’s left
are the memories,
and the flaking paint
and dying walls.

the house stands still-
a reminder of time gone soft:
a time of wealth and wonder,
of innocence
stitched into saturday mornings.

now,
it barely stands.
weathering the weather,
a far cry
from the majesty it once bore.

सुर्यलाई- के थाहा उ उदाइरहेको हो कि अस्ताइरहेको छ: सर्य उदाएपनि, उज्यालोमा आफ्नै छायाँ बिझ्छ, उज्यालोले कहिलेकाहीँ- हिउँले जस्तै पोल्छ, उसले छोडेको स्पर्शको याद बनेर। सुर्य अस्ताए पनि, उज्यालोको त्यो सम्झना- मलाई पनि,…

मन त आँफै-
यौटा समुन्द्र,
शब्दविहिन, तर-
लहरहरुले भरिएको,
न काहिँ थालिन्छ,
न काहीँ टुंगिन्छ।
मन त आफैं-
यसै चलायमान हुन्छ,
कसैको आदेशमा चल्दो रहेनछ,
कुनै बादलको ओढारजस्तो
आफ्नो डरबाटै बगिरहन्छ।

कतैबाट यौटा-
अनुहार देखा पर्छ
अस्पष्ट- अधुरो,
त्यो अनुहार-
तिम्रो हो कि मेरो
धुवाँलिएको आफ्नै प्रतिविम्ब
समयको ऐनाले खोपेको मुहार,
या सम्झनाका रहरहरू,
जुन मसँग छैन, तर
जसले मलाई हरेकपटक,
त्यही तलाउमा छाडी दिन्छ,
तलाउ नबोले पनि,
पग्लिरहेने समय।

सुर्यलाई-
के थाहा उ
उदाइरहेको हो कि
अस्ताइरहेको छ:
सर्य उदाएपनि,
उज्यालोमा आफ्नै छायाँ बिझ्छ,
उज्यालोले कहिलेकाहीँ-
हिउँले जस्तै पोल्छ,
उसको स्पर्शको याद बनेर।
सुर्य अस्ताए पनि,
उज्यालोको त्यो सम्झना-
मलाई पनि,
मेरो छायाँहरुमा पनि।

हावा चलिरहेको छ-
सँधै नै चलि रहन्छ,
हावाको कुनै सिमाना हुँदैन,
मन जस्तै- बगिरहने,
कहिले ठोस बन्न नसक्ने,
थाम्न खोज्दा झन बग्ने चाह।
तलाउलाइ आदेश-
दिन सकिन्न,
समयलाई-
थाम्न खोज्दा- खोज्दै
म त यसै
बग्न थालिसके छु।

म बगिरहेछु-
हावा जस्तै,
छायाँ जस्तै,
सम्झनाको धुवाँ जस्तै।
एकछिनलाई लाग्छ
उसलाइ एकफेर बोलाउने
मनभरिका सबैकुरा खोल्ने-
शब्दहरूको के अर्थ छ र
जब उसको त्यो आकृति
कहिल्यै स्पष्ट भएन।

तरल यो मन-
तलाउ नचलाए पनि
तलाउको गहिराइमा
डुबिरहने डर।
उसले भनेको मानेर-
म पनि त मौन नै बसेँ
तर मनले मानेन-
मौनता पनि उत्तर
हुन सक्छ, तर-
मौनतामा बाँच्न
सिकिसके पछि अब:
शब्दहरू- न्यानो रहेनन्
प्रश्नहरू- प्रश्न रहेनन।

तलाउको गहिराइ-
शून्यताको साक्षी,
उज्यालो भन्दा पुरानो,
बाँच्न भन्दा पहिले;
तलाउ बग्दैन, सुन्दैन
मौन आदेश दिइरहन्छ,
फेरि तलाउको शान्ति-
भत्काउन पनि त सक्दिन।
भित्र-
घनघोरको आँधीपूराणहरू,
केही पग्लिरहेको,
मलाई तानिरहेको,
जहाँ सम्झना सधैं-
विषाद बनि पोली रहन्छ।

समयसँगै-
सङ्लिन्छ सबै भन्थ्यौ,
तलाउमा डुब्न डराउँछु,
अनि शान्त तलाउभित्र,
सङ्लिन खोज्दा हराउँछु।
सङ्लिनु भनेको के हो-
हराउनु कि बाँच्नु?
समय त-
आफैं भुल्न सक्दो रहेनछ,
हराउनेहरू कहिले नबिर्सने,
समयले त-
मलाइ त्यतै बाँधि राखेछ,
अझैपनि विथोल्न छाडेको छैन।

शरीर-
स्थिर छ, तर,
मन- कहिल्यै रोकिँदैन
भित्र कतै उर्लिरहेको
देखिने आँधी-
नितान्त अदृश्य
घनघोरको आँधिपुराणहरू,
शब्दहरूमा– बोलिन्छ, लेखिन्छ,
उसले देखिन, मैले लुकाएँ।
रुन्छु, हाँस्छु, बग्छु
हावालाई बाँध्न सकिँदैन,
म भित्रको हावा,
कहिल्यै रोकिँदैन-
बगिरहेको छु,
थुनिइरहेको छु,
मेरो छायाँले-
कहिल्यै बिश्राम लिँदैन।

देशभक्ति; खुकुरीको धारसँगै चम्किएको थियो रे कुनैबेला, वीरहरूको गर्जनसँगै गर्जिएको थियो रे कुनैबेला, म, यति बेला इतिहास खाएर आफ्नो भोक टार्न सक्दिन, मलाई बलभद्रसँगै देशभक्तिले शाहदत पाएको थाह छ, मलाई अमरसिंहसँगै…

देशभक्ति देख्नेहरुले,
अलिकति, दौराको फेरमा
अल्झिएको देखे,
अलिकति, हिमालको टुप्पोमा
टल्किएको देखे,
अलिकति, स्वयम्भूको आँखामा
चम्किएको देखे,
अलिकति, नेताको भाषणमा
पस्किएको देखे,
देख्नेहरुले,
मान्छेको मनभित्र
सल्किएको पनि देखे!
देशभक्ति;
खै म कहाँ गएर भेटुँ,
छातीभित्र हुन्छ भन्छन्,
खै म कहाँ गएर देखुँ?

देशभक्ति;
खुकुरीको धारसँगै
चम्किएको थियो रे कुनैबेला,
वीरहरूको गर्जनसँगै
गर्जिएको थियो रे कुनैबेला,
म,
यति बेला इतिहास खाएर
आफ्नो भोक टार्न सक्दिन,
मलाई बलभद्रसँगै देशभक्तिले
शाहदत पाएको थाह छ,
मलाई अमरसिंहसँगै देशभक्तिले
अवकाश लिएको थाह छ,
मलाई भीमसेनसँगै देशभक्ति
सेरिएको पनि थाह छ।

चेतनाले ब्यूँझाइदिएको
देशभक्तिलाई,
थप्-थपाएर फेरी
सुत्न लगाएको मलाई थाह छ,
चस्मा जस्तै फुकालेर
देशभक्तिलाई,
मान्छेहरू मस्त सुतिरहेको-
मलाई थाह छ,
झन्डा तल बसेर,
देश बेचिरहेको पनि
मलाई थाह छ,
दौडन्छ भन्छन्
नशा-नशामा देशभक्ति,
सलबलाउँछ भन्छन्
रगत रगतमा देशभक्ति,
देशभक्ति बहने मैले
कुनै नशा देखेको छैन,
देशभक्ति कसैको रगतमा
सल्बलाएको देखेको छैन,
देशका लागि कसैले
साउती मारिरहेको देखेको छैन।

समय आएपछि देशभक्ति
फुल भएर फुल्छ भन्छन्,
सम्सानघाट भैसक्यो देश,
खै समय आएको छैन?
साना भंगेराहरु सधैँ जालमा परि रहे,
सुगाहरू सधैँ
पिञ्जरामा बन्द रहे,
पश्चिमी हावाका झोँकाले
कोपिलाहरू झरि रहे,
कोशी-कर्णाली
सधैँ रुँदै-रुँदै बहिरहे,
फेरी स्यालहरू
नयाँ स्वरमा कराइ रहे,
दक्षिण हावाहरू त्यसैगरि बहिरहे,
खै त, कसैमा पनि-
देशभक्ति जागृत भा ‘छैन ।

म यति बेला चुपचाप झ्यालबाट
टोलाइरहेको छु,
अनि सोच्दै छु;
देशभक्ति कुन चराको नाम हे,
खै कहाँ हुन्छ यो ।

नहरचोक, २००७।

बासभका अरू कविता: मौन प्रतिबिम्ब · कार्की दाई, राजा, गणतन्त्र · अनुत्तरित खल्दुलीहरू · सबै कविता ›

धुबाँ जस्तै- बिलायो समय अबशेष मात्र बाँकि; पुरानो सम्झना, के त्यो जीवन हो? कि स्मृतिको लहर? शायद प्रेमको, शायद अनुपस्थितिको। म शब्द बेच्दिनँ, केवल अनुभूति सुनाउँछु- मूल्य त- तिनैले तोक्छन्, जो महसुस गर्न सक्छन। घामको…

जीवन-

स्वप्न हो

कि यथार्थ-

कि हाम्रै

मस्तिष्कले

बनाएको जेल,

जहाँ हामी

सपनाको विपनामा

साँझलाई भेटाउँछौँ।

सस्तो-महँगो-

कस्तो, को,

के-को हो

यो मापन?

धत्, बिदाइ कति गार्हो हुन्छ है? म कतै धुवाँ बनेर उडिसकेको हुनेछु तिमीले यो पत्र पढ्दा। मेरो कमजोरीको समयमा, मेरो लागि पनि उर्जा दिएका थियौ तिमीले, यो पढेर पनि तिमी रुनेछैनौ भन्ने आशा गरेको छु। किन दु:ख मान्नु र, म त…

१.

२०१०, जुन।

एकाबिहानै फेसबुक खोल्नु मेरो दैनिकी नै भै सकेको थियो। रिकोमेन्डेड फ्रेन्डस को लिस्टमा यौटा अनौठो नाममा गएर आँखा टक्क अडियो। अना मिका, नयाँ ट्याब हतार हतार खोलेर, फ्रेन्ड रिक्वेस्टको निलो बटन क्लीक गरेर एकछिन उसको एक्टिभिटी नियाँले। कलेज सकेर केहि घन्टापछि, फेरी फेसबुक खोल्दा यौटा नोटिफिकेसन र यौटा म्यासेज आएको रहेछ। हेरेँ, त्यहि अनामिका अनलाइन रैछ, लैखिएको थियो, "हेल्लो बोधिसत्व।", ढिला नगरि रिपलाई गरेँ, "हाइ”।

टुप्लुक्क प्रश्न गरी, "सो, बुद्धु, की बुद्ध?", सोचेँ, फरासिली रहिछ।

बठ्याईँ देखाउँदै उत्तर दिएँ, "लेट्स गिभ अस सम टाइम, यु विल नो युरसेल्फ।"

एकफेर हाँसेझैँ गर्दै उसले भनि, "अनि, नाम चाहिँ प्रवेश होला हैन? बोधिसत्व त पक्कै भैसक्या छैन होला।"

"बोधिसत्व हुन दिएन सांसारीक सुख-सयनले, अहिले नाम मात्रै भएपनि राखौँ भनेर नि।”

अनि, "ए अनामिका, भन्न त कस्तो नमिल्दो रैछ क्या।", घुमाउरो पारामा नाम जान्न खोजेँ मैले।

"फर्मालिटि उफ्फ!" चिढीएझैँ गरि उसले थपि, "पल्पसा, पल्पसा काफ्ले",

"कसो, पल्पसा क्याफे भएन छौ" मैले भनेँ। रिसाओस् भनेर हतार-हतार यौटा स्माइली पनि थपिवरी म्यासेज पठाएँ।

"भएको भए के हुन्थ्यो र?" उ पनि कहाँ कम थिइ त।

"के थाह, मलाई तिमी पनि मन पर्न सक्थ्यो।" मैले टेस्टेस्टोरन फ्यूल्ड रिप्लाई दिएँ।

"तिमिलाई के बढी मन परेको? नारयण वाग्ले की उसले बनाएको पल्पसा?" प्रश्न सोझ्याएकि थिइ मलाइ।

"पल्पसा र दृश्यको केमिस्ट्रि।" बाठो उत्तर दिएँ।

"बाठो रहेछौ, दृश्य झैँ।" कम्प्लिमेन्ट हो कि अरु केही, बुझिन, मुस्कुराउँदै लेखेँ,

"तिमी, बरु ठ्याक्कै पल्पसा झैँ रहेछौ। आशावादी छु, हाम्रो मिलन वियोगान्त नहोस्।"

"हामी त्यस्तो वादमा किन अल्झनु पर्यो र?" झर्केर भनि उसले। एकछिन, घोरिएर फेरि पढि क्यार केही बेर, लेखि, "तिमी आफूलाई त्यहि दृश्य जस्तो ठान्छौ की?”

"म परिस्थितिमा बाँधिएको छु, मनमौजी छैन उसको जस्तो। फेरि मेरो क्रियटिभिटि भनेको गफीन मै सीमित हुन्छ।" मैले यथार्थ सुनाएँ।

"फिक्सन झैँ जिन्दगि कहाँ हुन्छ र?" उसले थपि, "त्यो पल्पसा जस्तो स्वदेशमा बसेर क्यामेरा बोकेर हिँड्न सकेको छैन, सिंगापुरमा कपडा काट्नु परेको छ।”

"दर्जी हो?" मैले रिङाउनलाई भनेँ।

"हैन, यहाँ फेसन डिजाइन पढिरहेको छु। तिमी के गर्छौ नी?” प्रतिप्रश्न तेर्स्याइ उसले।

“जेनेटीक इन्जिनियरिङमा ब्याचलर्स गर्दै छु, बंगलादेशमा।”

एक्कासि, भेट भएको थियो हाम्रो त्यो दिन। पहिलो पटकमै यसरी खुलेर कुरा सायदै कोही सँग गरेको थिए होला मैलै। तर, त्यो अन्तिम कुराकानी थिएन, बस सुरुवात थियो उसंगको मित्रताको, एक भारी सम्झनाहरूको।

२.

२०१०, नोभेम्बर।

हाम्रो कुराकानी प्राय बेलुका हुने गर्थ्यो। दिनभरि कलेजको थकाइ, अनि कुरा गर्ने अधैर्यता, कोठा पुगेर हतार हतार फेसबुक खोल्थेँ। फेसबुक खोल्न कम गार्हो हुन्थेन उसबेला। हतार हतार गर्दै ग्रामीनफोनको डङ्गल घुसाएर ल्यापटप मा फेसबुक खोल्दा उसैको म्यासेज टुङ्ग बजथ्यो।

केही दिन दैनिकी को बारेमा मुन्ड्यान वार्तालाप हुने गर्थे, विस्तारै हामी दर्शन, साहित्य, विज्ञान, धर्म, म्युजिक, स्पिरिचुलिटी, हेरेका सिनामाहरू, पढेका किताबहरु.. हरेक खाले र सबैखाले कुरा गर्न थालेका थियौं। पल्पसा क्याफेमा, नारायण दाइले पल्पसा को क्यारेक्टरमा न्याय गर्न सकेझैँ लाग्दैन थियो, यो पल्पसा सबै कुरामा मैले कल्पना गरेको उही पल्पसा झैँ लाग्न थालेको थियो, 'ट्यालेन्टेट, क्रियटिभ, मिलनसार, एक्स्ट्रोभर्ट' अनि त्यो भन्दा पनि बढि डाउन टु अर्थ। समयले अरुनै केहि निर्णय गर्यो, नभए, पक्कै एक सफल डिजाइनर हुने थिई होला।

म दृश्य थिइन, शब्दलाई पेपरको क्यानभासमा बेला बेला उतार्ने गरेको थिएँ। मनमौजी पक्कै थिइन, अलि अलि भएको स्वतन्त्रता पनि बंगलादेशको दुई वर्षमा कुण्ठित भै सकेको थिए। मलाई दृश्य मन परेन, अलि बढी हावादारी, इगोइस्ट र लापरवाह लाग्थ्यो। लथालिङ्ग त म जरुर थिएँ, घमन्डी कत्तिको थिएँ, अरूले जज गरिहाल्छन।

"प्रवेश, जीवन के हो जस्तो लाग्छ?" एक दिन एक्कासि प्रश्न गरेकी थिई पल्पसाले, "तिमिलाई आफूले पाएको यो समय प्रति जस्टिस गरेजस्तो लाग्छ त?

त्यसो त हामीले हरेक विषयमा कुरा गरिसकेको थियौँ। वैदिक गन्थन देखि जुलियन एसेन्जको “बहादुरी” को बहस गर्थ्यौ। गान्धी र मन्डेलाका शान्ति सन्देश, अनि सिकन्दर महान् र नेपोलियनका युद्धहरू, जनयुद्धको नेपाल, अनि जनयुद्धमा विनाकारण जेल मा बसिरहेको अन्तरको कथाहरू को कुरा गर्थ्यौँ। राम, जिसस र बुद्ध का प्रिन्सिपलहरू; अनि राधा, द्रौपदी, मेरी र यशोधराहरूले सहनु परेका कष्टहरू उद्धरण गर्दै, धर्म र धर्मको नाममा धर्म भिक्षुका कर्तुतहरू पर्दाफास गर्थ्यौं समय मिलेसम्म। इन्द्र, जिउस, अनि जरासुत्र को समानता, आर्यन इन्भेजन, हराएको सिन्धुघाँटीको सभ्यता, वेद देखि मनुस्म्रीती सम्म आएपुग्दा बहकिएको हाम्रो हिन्दु धर्म; लाग्थ्यो, हरेक विषयमा हाम्रो कुरा मिल्थ्यो। हैन, केही असमानता थिए हाम्रो, नत्र त पट्यार लाग्दो हुन्थ्यो होला हाम्रो मित्रता।

अनि, हेन्ड्रिक्सको गितार, लेनन र म्याककार्थीका ट्युन्स, बब डायलन र जोनी मिचेलका प्रेरणादायी लिरिक्स, अनि रे चार्लस र, अर्रिथा फ्रयाङ्कलिन का सोल सँग थिए हामी सँग, सँग-सँगै सुन्थ्यौँ। अँ, पिंक फ्लोयड अनि साइक्लेडिक म्युजिक सँग पनि उसैले परिचय गराएकी थिई मलाई। कति चाँडै कति धेरै कुरा गरिसकेका हामी, उसको प्रश्न गहिरो लाग्यो मलाई, खै किन हो।

तैपनि, हलुङ्गो उत्तर दिएको थिएँ, "मर्नु अघि हामीले बाँच्ने समय।" पछी थपेँ, "२०+ हुँदेछौँ भर्खर, अहिले नै कन्टेम्पलेट गर्न पर्छ जस्तो लाग्दैन पल्पसा मलाई। जीवन त धेरै लामो छ; भन्छ नि हामीले बाँचुन्जेल गर्ने सबैभन्दा लामो काम नै जिउनु हो।"

उसले गम्भीर हुँदै भनेको थिइ, "हेन्ड्रिक्स जस्तै जिन्दगी पो जिन्दगी त, २६ वर्षमै मरेर पनि गितारको लिजेन्ड भएको छ"

अनेपक्षित सिरियसनेस तिर मोडिएपछि मैले भनेको थिएँ, "हैन, मलाई त सिकन्दर हुनु छ, संसार जित्नु छ। सिकन्दर भन्दा फरक अन्त्य गर्नु छ जिन्दगीको।"

उसले साथ दिँदै भनेको थिइ, "डायरिया बाट बचेर इन्डिया पनि जित है यो पल्ट।" हाँसेका थियौँ दुबैजाना....

"विल यु वि ह्याप्पी, ह्वेन यु डाइ?" उसले सोधी।

इन्टरनेट सकिए छ क्यार, ल्यापटप बन्द गरेँ।

मोबाइलमा, 'लाइक अ रोलिङ स्टोन' सुन्दै सुतेको थिएँ त्यो रात।

केही महिना, दिनचर्या यसरी नै बित्दै थिए।

३.

२०११, फेब्रुअरी।

हिउँद अलि बढि नै चिसो थियो यो यामको। पल्पसाले म्यासेजको रिप्लाई नगरेको एक हप्ता जस्तो भएको थियो, मन अलि बढी नै अधीर हुँदै थियो। जाडोमा ठिहीले ओइलाएको बिरुवा जस्तै, यो जाडोमा, उसँग नबोल्दा मेरा दिनहरु पनि ओइलाएझैँ लाग्न थालेको थिए। एक किसिमले बानी परिसकेको रहेछ उ सँग कुरा गर्ने। अचम्मको हुने है बानी पनी, लाग्न गार्हो, लागेपछि छुट्न सार्हो। रिस पनि उठ्थ्यो बेला-बेला, केही भएर होला, त्यतिकै त हराउन नपर्ने भन्ठानेर चित्त बुझाउँथेँ।

उसको प्रोफाइल हेर्थैँ दिनहुँ, बेला बेला कता गायब भएको भन्दै म्यासेज गर्ने गर्थेँ, कता हराएको, मलाई बिर्स्यौ आदि इत्यादि... अहँ, केही उत्तर आएन। हप्तौसम्म रहिरह्यो शून्यता, कतै केही खबर आएन। थक्क थक्क लाग्न थालेको थियो, फोन नम्बर, इमेल लिएको भए पनि हुन्थ्यो नि भन्दै; अस्ति-अस्ति त्यसको आवश्यक्ता पनि महसुस भएको थिएन नी।

झन्डै एक महिना बितेको थियो, पल्पसा हराएकी। एक दिन नचिनेको नामबाट म्यासेज आएको देखेँ, उसैकी बहिनीले गरेकी रहिछे,”दाइ पल्पसाले हजुरको लागि यौटा चिठ्ठी छाडेकी छ, मैले स्क्यान गरेर पठाएको छु है" भन्दै, एट्याजमेन्ट पढ्न थालेँ।

"

बोधिसत्व नभैसकेको प्यारो प्रवेश,

सुरुमा, सरी भनेर यो पत्र लेख्न सुरु गर्दैछु। यो पत्र पाउँदा तिमीलाई केही पनि थाह नदिइ हराएको हुनेछु म, तिमीले पाउने कष्ट, तिमीले पाउने तनाव, र पक्कै रिसाका हुनेछौ, माफी माग्छु म, मेरो विवशता थियो सब। तिमीसँग कुरा गरेर मैले ४-५ महिना बिताएँ होला। तिमीले फेसबुकको सजेसनमा मलाई नदेखेको भए, देखेर पनि फ्रेन्ड रिक्वेस्ट नपठाएको भए, मैले पनि त जो पायो तेही भन्दै तिमीलाई इग्नोर गर्न सक्थेँ। यी सब संयोगहरू नभएको भए कति अपूरो हुने रहेछ मेरा यी आखिरी दिनहरू।

हो प्रवेश, मैले आफ्नोबारे सबैकुरा भनेको थिइन मैले। तिमीसँग भेट्दा नै लगभग थाह भैसकेको मलाई, म मर्न आँटेकी थिए। तिमी सँग भेट भयो, मेरो ट्रान्जिसन सहज भयो। जम्मा-जम्मी २२ वर्ष बसेँ यो संसारमा, गर्न पर्ने र गर्नै सोचेको कामहरू कत्ति थिए कत्ति। म खासमा सार्है डराएकी थिएँ, सुरू-सुरूमा- मरेर, सबैकुरा र सबैलाई छाडेर जान कहाँ सहज हुन्थ्यो र। तिमीसँग गरेका कुराकानीहरू मेरा लागि पेन किलर थिए, कहिले लागेन चाँडै मर्नेवाला छु, ब्रेनट्युमर त के, माइग्रेन छ जस्तो पनि लागेन कहिले। सायद भनेको भए तिम्रो र मेरो सम्बन्ध अर्कै हुन्थ्यो होला कि सोचेर केहि पनि भनिन मैले तिमीलाई। सायद तिमी मलाई यौटी मर्न लागेको केटीको नजरले हेर्थ्यौ होला, हाम्रो च्याटहरूमा ख्याल ठट्टा भन्दा बढी सान्त्वनाका शब्द हुन्थ्यो होला।

हो म स्वार्थी भएँ। म सिकन्दर वा हेन्ड्रिक्स हुन सकिन, तर मर्नु अघि टन्नै सम्झनाहरू लिएर जान चाहन्थेँ। मैले कैले पुनर्रजन्ममा विश्वास गरीनँ, मलाई थाह छ तिमी म भन्दा बढी एग्नोस्टिक छौँ, यिनै शब्दहरूनै हाम्रो आखिरी भेट, तिम्रो लागि मेरो आखिरी सम्झना। यु आर अ भेरी गुड म्यान प्रवेश, स्मार्ट, क्रियटिभ, अनि डाउन टु अर्थ। हाम्रा ख्याल ठट्टा, ती गम्भिर डिबेट्स, म तिम्रो सबैकुरामा भएको नलेज को कायल थिएँ म। आशा गर्छु यु विल डु जस्टिस टु इट, याद छ, सिकन्दर बन्नु छ तिमीलाई, करेजको अफ़ग़ानिस्तान कटेर सपनाहरूको इन्डीया पनि जित्न बाँकी छ।भनिन्छ नि शिखर चड्न हिंडेको मान्छे, फेदिमै अल्मलियो भने, उसले शिखर कहिल्यै टेक्दैन। आशा छ, हिँड्न छाड्दैनौँ, बाटो बिर्सदैनौँ।

जब म हस्पिटलको बेडमा थला परेर बसेको हुनेछु, मलाई थाह छ आइ विल मिस यु टेरिब्ली। पल्पसा क्याफेको त्यो "झरी' भन्ने पेन्टिङ याद छ? म त्यसरीनै झरिरहेको हुनेछु, सायद प्रेम गर्न थालेछु तिमीलाई, थाह नपाइ। कस्तो कमजोर हुन्छ है मन, मर्छु भन्दा भन्दै पनि रोक्न नसकिने। भेट भएन है हाम्रो, बेला बेला कल्पना गर्छु, भेट भए के गर्थेँ होला भनेर। अहिले, शब्दहरू मात्रै भएपनि लिएर-छाडेर जाँदैछु।

धत्, बिदाइ कति गार्हो हुन्छ है? म कतै धुवाँ बनेर उडिसकेको हुनेछु तिमीले यो पत्र पढ्दा। मेरो कमजोरीको समयमा, मेरो लागि पनि उर्जा दिएका थियौ तिमीले, यो पढेर पनि तिमी रुनेछैनौ भन्ने आशा गरेको छु। किन दु:ख मान्नु र, म त विगत हुँ, केही दिन कुरा भयो, रमाइलो भयो, होपफुल्ली यु इन्जोएड माई कम्पनि एस मच एस आइ डीड। तिमीसँग त सारा जिन्दगी छ, जिउनलाई, म जस्ता अरू कति भेट्छौ भेट्छौ तिमीले। मेरो यौटा इच्छा छ, सक्छौ भने बिर्सीदेउ मलाई, होइन भने तिम्रो कथामा कतै यौटा पात्र बनाइदेउ, तिम्री अनामिका जस्तै।
